Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY 2010 PILG GOVERNOR ROBERT ACE S. BARBERS Provincial Capitol Building Province of Surigao del Norte Dear Governor Barbers: This has reference to your letter dated 11 March 2010 requesting this Department to revisit and review its earlier opinions addressed to several mayors •of Surigao del Norte regarding the use of the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) of Congressman Francisco T. Matugas as intelligence fund to bolster the peace and order campaign in their respective localities. It may be recalled that in DILG Opinion Nos. 42 and 68, both series of 2009, and DILG Opinion No. 11, series of 2010, we categorically stated therein that if peace and order is a priority investment area in a local government unit, an allocation for peace and order concerns may already be provided in those LGU's respective annual budgets. However, in the case of the different municipalities of Surigao del Norte, Congressman Matugas has allocated funds to these municipalities, out of his PDAF, to be used as intelligence or anti-insurgency funds. In the aforesaid letters of the different mayors in Surigao del Norte, it was represented to us that the intelligence or anti-insurgency funds will be used in direct response to the operations of the New People's Army (NPA) in their respective localities which danger still looms up to the date of their respective letters. In the assailed DILG Opinions, we consistently opined that there is no legal impediment to such allocation for intelligence or anti-insurgency purposes from Congressman Matugas' PDAF as the same may be considered as a "trust fund" which is allowed under the law. In said DILG Opinions, we emphasized therein that the municipal mayors, as trustees of the fund, will "xxx hold and administer such funds to finance the activities to be done in furtherance to the purpose upon which the said trust fund was created subject to the usual auditing and accounting rules" According to you, the Mayors can possibly abuse such intelligence or anti- insurgency funds so that it can be a clear violation of the provisions of RA 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. We understand your predicament. However, we reiterate that trust funds, to which we categorized the allocation for intelligence or anti-insurgency purposes by Congressman Matugas out of his PDAF, are allowed under Section 309 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), viz:

"SECTION 309. special Funds.—There shall be maintained in every provincial, city, or municipal treasury the following special funds: (b) Trust funds which shall consist of private and public monies which have omcially come into the possession of the local government or of a local government official as trustee, agent or administrator, or which have been received as a guaranty for the fulfillment of some obligation. A trust fund shall only be used for the specific purpose for which it was created or for which it came into the possession of the local government unit." As to your predicament that such trust fund can be abused by concerned local chief executive and thus not for the specific purpose for which it came into his possession, we are of the view that such matter is already within the ambit of authority of the Commission on Audit (COA). Let it be noted that under Section 2 (1), Article IX (D) of the 1987 Constitution, COA has the power, authority, and duty to examine and audit all accounts pertaining to the receipts of and expenditures or uses of funds held in trust by, or pertaining to, the Government, or any of its subdivisions, agencies, instrumentalities. Hence, such trust fund should comply with the General Appropriations Act (GAA) and subject to the usual auditing and accounting rules as we have emphasized in our assailed DILG Opinions. As to the issue on the usage by the congressmen of the PDAF only to their priority development projects, as we mentioned in the immediately preceding paragraph, the General Appropriations Act governs the use of PDAF by the congressmen and one of the priority projects therein for which the PDAF may be used is for Peace and Order. As to whether intelligence or anti-insurgency purposes be considered a priority development project of congressmen, specifically Congressman Matugas, we are of the view that this is already a matter of discretion of Congressman Matugas which this Department cannot interfere nor question. "Discretion" is defined as "the freedom to act according to one's own judgment; unrestrained exercise of choice or will" (Moreno, Philippine Law Dictionary, p. 181). Finally, as to the issue on the use of the subject intelligence or anti- insurgency in other legislative districts, we shall refer the same to the Department of Budget and Management-Region XIII for appropriate action. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. JESU B DOQU Director II al Service Copy furnished: Regional Director Rene K.
